runs.reason: Observed: ALT-4AF3D618FAA9 reports 17752 flows and 173643 packets in one minute from one source toward one destination port, with repeated high-volume alerts including ALT-9941B48CD40E and ALT-5716F9F63616. Sampled flows FLOW-745C5543C223 and FLOW-8FC7C816EF4A show traffic from 172.16.0.1 to 192.168.10.50 on port 80. Inference: the sustained concentrated traffic supports a suspected flooding attack, but service disruption and malicious intent are not established by flow evidence alone.

findings.observation: The detection reports repeated high-volume one-minute groups targeting one destination port from one source.
Sampled records show the same source and destination communicating on destination port 80 at successive alert timestamps.

technique_mappings.reason: The DoS alert and flow volume do not establish denial-of-service impact; the alert reports one source, so a distributed attack mapping is unsupported.

next_steps.reason: Inspect the repeated port 80 traffic for request patterns and connection behavior that could distinguish flooding from legitimate activity.
Correlate sustained high-volume alerts with service health and authorized activity. This DoS incident requires explicit analyst confirmation before closure.

runs.limitations: Sampled flows cannot establish service availability, application behavior, or intent. Incident metadata describes a one-minute window while alerts span multiple minutes; statistics clarify that the aggregate flow count is a case sum. Analyst validation of the timeline and service impact remains necessary.
